5. Grammatical variations and cognate expressions

Legislation CitatorView Legislation Citator

Where any word or expression is defined in any Ordinance, such definition shall extend to the grammatical variations and cognate expressions of such word or expression.



[5.01] Enactment history

This section is originated in 1966 (originally 31 of 1966) commencing 31 December 1966.

[5.02] Cases

This section was considered in Ngai Po Lun Paul v Chan Cheryl [1990] 2 HKC 291 (CA). In this case, the court allowed a purported affirmation which did not conform with the requirements of s 7(4) of the Oaths and Declarations Ordinance (Cap 11) to be used as evidence.


6. References to Government property

Legislation CitatorView Legislation Citator
  • (1)Where reference is made in any Ordinance to property and the expressions used in relation thereto imply that the property is owned by, belongs to, or reverts to, the Government, or convey a similar meaning, the reference shall be construed in accordance with Article 7 of the Basic Law.
  • (2)In this section, property ( 財產) means any of the land and natural resources within the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

    (Replaced 26 of 1998 s. 6)



[6.01] Enactment history

This section was replaced by s 6 of the Adaptation of Laws (Interpretive Provisions) Ordinance 1998 (26 of 1998) which received Assent on 16 April 1998 and was deemed to have come into operation on 1 July 1997.


7. Provisions for gender and number

Legislation CitatorView Legislation Citator
  • (1)Words and expressions importing the masculine gender include the feminine and neuter genders. (Amended 89 of 1993 s. 4)
  • (2)Words and expressions in the singular include the plural and words and expressions in the plural include the singular.


[7.01] Enactment history

This section was amended by the Interpretation and General Clauses (Amendment) (No 2) Ordinance 1993 (89 of 1993), s 4 which came into operation on 17 December 1993.

[7.02] General note

Section 7(2) is frequently referred to in cases. See [7.05] below.

[7.03] Commonwealth of Australia

Compare this section with s 23 of Acts Interpretation Act 1901 which provides:

In any Act, unless the contrary intention appears:

  • (a)words importing a gender include every other gender; and
  • (b)words in the singular number include the plural and words in the plural number include the singular.

[7.04] UK

There was a similar provision in s 6 of the Interpretation Act 1978:

In any Act, unless the contrary intention appears,

  • (a)words importing the masculine gender include the feminine;
  • (b)words importing the feminine gender include the masculine;
  • (c)words in the singular include the plural and words in the plural include the singular.
